questions.md: An optical fibre with core refractive index 1.80 is to be cladded so that the refracted light ray grazes the interface. The fibre will contain light travelling within 10° of the fibre axis when it is placed in air. What minimum refractive index is allowed for the cladding? If the same fibre is placed in water (refractive index 1.33), find the acceptance angle and numerical aperture.
With the necessary diagram, obtain an expression for the angle of acceptance and the numerical aperture of an optical fibre.
With a necessary diagram, derive an expression for the angle of acceptance and the numerical aperture.
Derive the relation between the different Einstein coefficients at thermal equilibrium. Discuss the nature of emission for $hf \ll kT$.

An atom has two energy levels with a transition wavelength of 582 nm. At 300 K, $4.0 \times 10^{20}$ atoms are in the lower state.

(a) How many occupy the upper state under thermal equilibrium?

(b) Suppose instead that $7.0 \times 10^{20}$ atoms are pumped into the upper state, with $4.0 \times 10^{20}$ atoms in the lower state. How much energy could be released in a single laser pulse?

A three-level laser emits light of wavelength 550 nm.

(a) What is the ratio of the population of the upper level ($E_2$) to that of the lower level ($E_1$) in the laser transition at 300 K?

(b) At what temperature does the ratio of the population of $E_2$ to that of $E_1$ become half?

$V_1$ and $V_2$ are the stopping potentials for light of two different frequencies $
u_1$ and $
u_2$ ($
u_2 > 
u_1 > 
u_0$) respectively, incident on a photoemissive surface. Is the relation $V_1 < V_2$ TRUE or FALSE? Justify your answer.

A tungsten cathode with a threshold wavelength of 435 nm is irradiated by ultraviolet light of wavelength 215 nm. Calculate (i) the maximum energy of the emitted photoelectrons and (ii) the work function of tungsten (in eV).

If the frequency of the incident radiation is increased beyond the threshold while the intensity is kept constant, what happens to:

(i) the number of emitted electrons, and

(ii) their kinetic energy?
A 30 eV electron and a 30 eV proton are incident on a square barrier of height 40 eV. What is the probability that the electron and the proton will tunnel through the barrier if its width is 0.10 nm?
Increasing the mass of a particle enhances its tunnelling probability for a fixed barrier. State whether the statement is True or False. Justify your answer.

A 30 eV electron is incident on a square barrier of height 40 eV. What is the probability that the electron tunnels through the barrier if its width is 0.1 nm? How does this change when the width is doubled and the energy is halved?

questions.skill: Particle in a box minimum energy
questions.md: A 0.50 kg baseball is confined between two rigid walls of a stadium that can be modelled as a "box" of length 100 m. Calculate the minimum speed of the baseball.
Solve the Schrödinger equation for a particle of mass $m$ in a one-dimensional infinite potential well (box) of length $L$ and obtain an expression for the wavefunction of the particle.
Apply the Schrödinger equation to a particle in a one-dimensional "box" of length $L$ and obtain the energy values of the particle.

questions.skill: Acceptability of wavefunction in finite well
questions.md: State whether the wavefunction $\psi = A e^{Cx}$ for $x \le 0$ is physically acceptable or not in the finite potential well with finite height $U$ and length $L$. Justify your answer.

Obtain the general solution of the Schrödinger equation for a particle of mass $m$ in a finite potential well of height $U$ and length $L$. Mention the boundary conditions needed to solve this system. Sketch the probability density for the lowest two energy states.

Well-1 and Well-2 are two square wells of the same length. Well-1 has walls of finite height and Well-2 has walls of infinite height. Each contains an identical quantum particle. Compare the magnitudes of the ground-state momenta.

What are the factors on which the electric field at some point P near a dipole in a dielectric material depends? Obtain a relationship between the polarizability and the relative permittivity of dielectric materials.

The atomic weight of Si is 28, its density is 2.33 g cm$^{-3}$ and each atom has a polarizability of $2 \times 10^{-40}$ F m$^2$. Calculate the ratio of the internal field to the external field in Si. Given $\varepsilon_0 = 8.854 \times 10^{-12}$ F/m.
A dielectric material has $\varepsilon_r = 4.94$ and $n^2 = 2.69$. Calculate the ratio between the electronic and ionic polarizability of this material.

A student conducted a photoelectric effect experiment by shining light of various wavelengths onto a metal surface. To stop the photocurrent, the student applied a negative potential until the current dropped to zero. The following readings were recorded. Are these readings valid? Justify your answer.

| Wavelength (nm) | Stopping potential (V) |
|---|---|
| 400 | 1.71 |
| 450 | 1.08 |
| 500 | 0.86 |
| 550 | 1.36 |

A student conducted a photoelectric effect experiment by shining light of wavelength 500 nm onto a metal surface. To stop the photocurrent, the student applied a negative potential until the current dropped to zero. He repeated the experiment while varying the distance of the light source (no other changes to the setup). How do these variations in distance affect the stopping potential and the photocurrent? Justify your answer.
When a free electron scatters a 0.854 nm X-ray photon, the electron recoils with a speed of $1.48 \times 10^{6}$ m/s. What is the resulting Compton shift in the photon's wavelength?

Analyse the relationship between the scattering angle and the wavelength shift when a metal target is exposed to extremely intense, monochromatic electromagnetic radiation, and discuss the physical significance of the Compton effect.
Define (i) group speed and (ii) phase speed. Show that for a non-relativistic quantum particle, the group speed of the wave packet equals the particle speed.
Define (i) group speed and (ii) phase speed of a wave packet. Show that the group speed of a wave packet equals the particle speed for a free non-relativistic quantum particle.
With the help of a schematic diagram, describe how the Davisson–Germer experiment confirmed the wave nature of electrons.
Illustrate the de Broglie concept of the wave properties of particles.

A quantum simple harmonic oscillator consists of an electron bound by a restoring force proportional to its displacement relative to an equilibrium position. A photon of 550 nm is used to excite the oscillator from the ground state to its first excited state. Calculate the proportionality constant and the energy of the first excited state.
